factual_claims.claim: Business loans increased 27% to €986 million, and home and other private loans grew 17% to €863 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Managing Director's Statement: 'The business loan portfolio grew the fastest, increasing by €207 million (+27%). This was followed by growth in the home loan portfolio by €125 million (+17%).' Note 4 segment data aligns with these figures.

factual_claims.claim: Customer deposits rose 9% to €2.05 billion, with demand deposits up 11% and term deposits up 8%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Page 13: 'Coop Pank’s deposits increased by 9% over the year, reaching 2.05 billion euros by the end of 2025. Term deposits increased by 8% over the year, while demand deposits increased by 11%.'

factual_claims.claim: The customer base increased by 19,000, or 9%, to 227,000.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Page 13: 'By the end of 2025 Coop Pank had 227,000 customers. In a year, the number of customers had increased by 19,000.'

factual_claims.claim: The operating environment improved as Estonia’s economy returned to modest growth, inflation receded and interest rates declined.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating Environment section (pages 7-8): Details modest GDP growth, falling inflation, and declining interest rates.

factual_claims.claim: Estonian home and business lending grew approximately 10% market-wide, supporting demand for Coop Pank’s financing products, but falling rates constrained the bank’s interest income.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Managing Director's Statement: 'in 2025, the volume of both home and business loans grew by approximately 10% market-wide... The decline in net profit... was mainly caused by the lower-interest economic environment.'

factual_claims.claim: The bank strengthened funding by issuing €250 million of four-year covered bonds, its first international covered-bond issuance, and began reducing more expensive term and foreign deposits.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Page 10: 'In the first quarter of 2025, Coop Pank issued covered bonds on the Irish stock exchange for the first time, amounting to €250 million with a four-year maturity... This stable long-term funding allowed the bank to begin intentionally reducing the volume of more expensive term and foreign deposits.'

factual_claims.claim: It also entered into an EIB Group guarantee arrangement expected to enable up to €249 million of new business lending, while a €5 million EEEF subordinated loan was drawn in February 2026.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Page 10: 'At the end of the year, Coop Pank entered into a guarantee agreement with the European Investment Bank Group... enabling the bank to issue up to €249 million in new loans... Additionally, Coop Pank signed a loan agreement... with the European Energy Efficiency Fund (EEEF), under which the bank will take an unsecured subordinated loan of €5 million...'

factual_claims.claim: Moody’s affirmed the bank’s Baa2 deposit rating with a positive outlook.

factual_claims.source_evidence: Page 10: 'In 2025, the credit rating agency Moody’s affirmed Coop Pank’s deposit rating at Baa2 with a positive outlook.'
